docs.title: vexy-paraltext
docs.text:
vexy-paraltext turns a folder of translated editions of one book into a single TMX translation memory of aligned sentences. You give it the English PDF, the German EPUB and the French DjVu of the same book. It gives you back book.tmx, where each translation unit holds one sentence and its counterparts in the other editions.

The tool runs locally. Text extraction uses command-line converters, sentence vectors come from local GGUF embedding models run through llama.cpp, and an optional clean-up pass talks to a local LLM served by LM Studio.

docs.title: What goes in, what comes out
docs.text:
A book folder holds one subfolder per language, named with the language code. Each subfolder holds one edition:

book/
  en/Book.pdf
  de/Buch.epub
  fr/Livre.djvu

After vexy-paraltext run book, the folder looks like this:

book/
  en/Book.pdf
  en/Book.md            stage 1: converter markdown, next to the source
  en/Book.norm.md       stage 2: LLM-normalized text (only when normalize is enabled)
  de/...
  fr/...
  paraltext-cache/      diskcache of LLM chunks and sentence vectors, converter scratch
  book.tmx              stage 4: the translation memory

The TMX file is named after the book folder: book/ produces book/book.tmx.

docs.title: Which sentences end up in the TMX
docs.text:
One edition is the pivot (English by default). A translation unit is written when a pivot sentence aligns in at least min_langs editions, counting the pivot itself. The default is min_langs = 2.

Follow one example through. The English edition has sentences A, B and C. The German edition has A, B and C. The French edition has only A and C. With the default setting, the TMX contains:

  • A in English, German and French
  • B in English and German
  • C in English, German and French

Sentences with no counterpart in any other edition are dropped. Units are never padded with empty segments. Raise min_langs to require more editions per unit.

docs.title: The four stages
docs.text:
stage command input output 1. Convert convert PDF, EPUB or DjVu <lang>/<stem>.md 2. Normalize normalize <stem>.md <lang>/<stem>.norm.md 3. Embed embed sentences of each edition vectors in paraltext-cache/ 4. Align align vectors of all editions <book>.tmx

run chains all four. Each stage reuses what the previous run left on disk, so a second run only redoes work whose inputs changed. See How it works for what happens inside each stage.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Installation: the package and the external converters.
  • Quickstart: build your first TMX.
  • Command line: every command and option.
  • Configuration: the paraltext.toml file.
  • Embedding models: which model to choose and why.
  • TMX output: the file format the tool writes.
  • Troubleshooting: common failures and their fixes.
  • Development: tests, builds and releases.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
vexy-paraltext COMMAND BOOK_DIR [OPTIONS]

The command line is built with Python Fire. Options can be written with dashes or underscores (--min-langs 3 or --min_langs 3). Boolean options are switched on by naming them (--force, --verbose).

Run vexy-paraltext COMMAND --help for the generated help of one command.

Generated help text

Some docstrings behind the generated help predate the current layout. Where they differ from this page, this page follows the code: stage outputs are written next to the sources and into paraltext-cache/, not into .paraltext/, and --min-langs defaults to 2, not to all editions.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
command does convert Stage 1: converts every edition to markdown. normalize Stage 2: cleans the markdown with a local LLM. embed Stage 3: computes sentence vectors into the cache. align Stage 4: aligns sentences and writes the TMX. run All four stages in order. batch run on every book folder under a root folder.

align and embed read the output of earlier stages. If the markdown of an edition is missing, they fail with run convert/normalize first. align runs embed itself; vectors already in the cache are reused.

docs.title: Options shared by all commands
docs.text: option default meaning --config PATH search order, see Configuration Use this paraltext.toml instead of searching for one. --verbose off Log at debug level (DEBUG instead of INFO), to stderr.

docs.title: convert
docs.text:
vexy-paraltext convert BOOK_DIR [--force] [--config PATH] [--verbose]

Converts each language folder's PDF, EPUB or DjVu to <stem>.md next to the source. Existing markdown is kept unless you pass --force. Prints the paths of the markdown files.

An edition that cannot be converted is logged as an error and skipped. The book fails only if fewer than two editions remain at the align stage.

docs.title: normalize
docs.text:
vexy-paraltext normalize BOOK_DIR [--force] [--config PATH] [--verbose]

Sends the markdown, chunk by chunk, to an OpenAI-compatible chat server and writes <stem>.norm.md. Existing .norm.md files are kept unless you pass --force. When [normalize] enabled = false, the command does nothing and the later stages read the raw <stem>.md.

docs.title: embed
docs.text:
vexy-paraltext embed BOOK_DIR [--model NAME] [--limit N]
                     [--backend NAME] [--dimensions N] [--precision NAME]
                     [--config PATH] [--verbose]

Splits each edition into sentences and embeds every sentence plus every pair of adjacent sentences. Vectors are stored in <book>/paraltext-cache/cache/embeddings. Prints one line per language: en: 14439 sentences embedded.

option meaning --model NAME A model profile from the config (jina, gemma, granite, ...) or the path of a GGUF file that a profile declares. Default: [embed] model, which is jina. --limit N Use only the first N sentences of each edition. For development. --backend NAME Override the backend of the selected profile, for example jina to use the Jina API instead of the local GGUF. For the jina and voyage backends, the profile's prompt prefix is dropped. --dimensions N Override [embed] dimensions. --precision NAME Override [embed] precision: float32, int8, int4 or binary.

A GGUF path that no profile declares is rejected. Add a profile for it in paraltext.toml first (see Configuration).

docs.title: align
docs.text:
vexy-paraltext align BOOK_DIR [--model NAME] [--pivot LANG] [--threshold X]
                     [--min-langs N] [--limit N] [--out PATH]
                     [--backend NAME] [--dimensions N] [--precision NAME]
                     [--config PATH] [--verbose]

Aligns every edition against the pivot and writes the TMX. Prints <units> units -> <path>.

option default meaning --pivot LANG pivot in config, else en if present, else the first edition Source language of the alignment. --threshold X [embed] threshold = 1.05 Margin-score cutoff. Higher keeps fewer, cleaner pairs. --min-langs N min_langs = 2 Keep a unit when at least N editions align, the pivot included. --limit N none Use only the first N sentences of each edition. --out PATH <book_dir>/<book_dir name>.tmx Where to write the TMX.

--model, --backend, --dimensions and --precision work as for embed.

docs.title: run
docs.text:
vexy-paraltext run BOOK_DIR [all align options] [--force]

Runs convert, normalize and align (which embeds). --force redoes conversion and normalization; vectors already cached are still reused.

docs.title: batch
docs.text:
vexy-paraltext batch ROOT [--config PATH] [--verbose]

Runs run on every subfolder of ROOT whose name does not start with a dot, in alphabetical order. It prints each book's result line. An exception in one book is logged with the book's folder name and the batch moves on.

batch uses the default alignment settings plus whatever the configuration sets. To pass a config to every book, use --config; otherwise each book uses its own paraltext.toml, if present.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Everything, with the Gemma model, requiring three editions per unit
vexy-paraltext run mybook --model gemma --min-langs 3

# Re-convert after replacing a PDF
vexy-paraltext convert mybook --force

# German as pivot, output elsewhere
vexy-paraltext align mybook --pivot de --out ~/tm/mybook-de.tmx

# Use a specific config file and debug logging
vexy-paraltext run mybook --config ~/paraltext.toml --verbose

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Settings live in a TOML file named paraltext.toml. Every key is optional; a missing key keeps its built-in default. Command-line options override the file for one call.

docs.title: Where the file is found
docs.text:
Without --config, the tool checks these locations in order and uses the first file it finds. Files are not merged.

  1. <book_dir>/paraltext.toml
  2. ./paraltext.toml in the current working directory
  3. ~/.config/vexy-paraltext/paraltext.toml

With --config PATH, only that file is read. If it does not exist, the defaults apply.

The repository ships an annotated example, paraltext.example.toml. Copy it and edit what you need.

cache_dir in the example file

The example file sets cache_dir = ".paraltext". The built-in default is paraltext-cache. If you copy the example unchanged, the cache goes into the hidden folder <book>/.paraltext/. Delete that line to keep the default.

docs.title: Top-level keys
docs.text: key default meaning pivot none Source language of the alignment. Without it, en is used if present, else the first edition. min_langs 2 A unit is kept when the pivot sentence aligns in at least this many editions, the pivot included. cache_dir "paraltext-cache" Folder inside the book folder for diskcache data and converter scratch files.

docs.title: [convert]
docs.text: key default meaning epub2md "~/bin/epub2md.py" Path of the EPUB converter script. The VEXY_EPUB2MD environment variable takes precedence. workers 3 Editions converted in parallel. Scanned editions that need OCR always run one at a time.

docs.title: [normalize]
docs.text:
The normalize stage sends the converter markdown to an OpenAI-compatible chat-completion server, such as LM Studio. It rewrites each chunk into plain paragraphs of complete sentences.

key default meaning enabled true false skips the stage; later stages read the raw <stem>.md. model "gemma-4-26b-a4b-it-qat-mxfp8" Model id as served by the chat server. base_url "http://localhost:1234/v1" Server base URL. Requests go to <base_url>/chat/completions. workers 4 Concurrent requests. chunk_chars 3000 Maximum characters per chunk. Chunks break on paragraph boundaries. max_tokens 2500 Maximum tokens per answer. temperature 0.1 Sampling temperature. timeout 1800.0 Request timeout in seconds.

The stage is slow with a large model. With gemma-4-26b-a4b-it-qat-mxfp8 on an M-series Mac, one illustrated book edition took about two hours; four concurrent requests doubled throughput compared with one, eight did not help further. With enabled = false the same book took about five minutes end to end.

docs.title: [embed]
docs.text: key default meaning model "jina" Profile name from [embed.models], or a GGUF path that a profile declares. threshold 1.05 Margin-score cutoff for alignment. Higher keeps fewer, cleaner pairs. gap_min_cos 0.6 Cosine similarity needed to pair a lone sentence between two aligned links. center true Subtract the joint mean vector before mining. Needed for Granite; helps the other models too. dimensions none Output dimensions. Omit for the model's full size. precision "int8" How vectors are stored in the cache: float32, int8, int4 or binary. max_tokens 512 Token limit per text, capped further by each model's context. batch_tokens 4096 Total llama.cpp batch budget. batch_size 32 Texts per batch.

docs.title: [embed.models.<name>]
docs.text:
Each table declares a model profile that --model <name> or [embed] model can select. Profiles in the file are added to the built-in ones; a profile with the same name replaces the built-in one completely. Keys you leave out take the defaults below, not the built-in profile's values, so restate prefix when you only want to change path.

key default meaning path "" GGUF file, for the llama.cpp backend. ~ is expanded. prefix none Text put in front of every sentence before embedding. model "" Model name passed to the uubed engine. Defaults to the profile name. backend "llama.cpp" Inference backend, for example llama.cpp, sentence-transformers, mlx, jina, voyage, cloudflare, hf or openai. device "mps" Device for local backends. endpoint none URL for the openai backend.

Built-in profiles:

name backend model file or name jina llama.cpp ~/.lmstudio/models/jinaai/jina-embeddings-v5-text-nano-text-matching/v5-nano-text-matching-Q8_0.gguf, prefix Query: gemma llama.cpp ~/.lmstudio/models/mntcloud/embeddinggemma-300m-Q8_0-better-gguf/embeddinggemma-300M-Q8_0.gguf, prefix task: sentence similarity \| query: granite llama.cpp ~/.lmstudio/models/mykor/granite-embedding-311m-multilingual-r2-GGUF/granite-embedding-311M-multilingual-r2-Q8_0.gguf, no prefix nomic sentence-transformers nomic minilm sentence-transformers minilm voyage-nano sentence-transformers voyage-nano voyage-lite voyage voyage-lite

API backends read their keys from the environment, never from the config file. The example file names them: JINA_API_KEY for jina, VOYAGE_API_KEY for voyage, CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN and CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID for cloudflare, HF_TOKEN for hf.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
A configuration for a collection on an external drive, with German as pivot, three editions per unit and the LLM stage off:

pivot = "de"
min_langs = 3

[normalize]
enabled = false

[embed]
model = "granite"
threshold = 1.05

[embed.models.granite]
path = "/Volumes/Models/granite-embedding-311M-multilingual-r2-Q8_0.gguf"
prefix = ""

docs.title: Cache keys
docs.text:
The cache invalidates itself when its inputs change:

  • Normalized chunks are keyed by the chat model id, the prompt version and the chunk text.
  • Sentence vectors are keyed by the embedding engine's identity, which includes the model and its settings, and by the sentence text. A changed segmentation only embeds the new sentences.

docs.title: Set up
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-paraltext.git
cd vexy-paraltext
uv sync --all-groups

Dependency groups: test (pytest, pytest-cov), lint (ruff, ty) and ocr (docling).

docs.title: Tests and checks
docs.text:
./test.sh

test.sh creates .venv with the test and lint groups if needed, installs the package in editable mode, and runs, in order:

  1. pytest, with a coverage floor of 80% (--cov-fail-under=80).
  2. ruff check src tests.
  3. ty check src.

The tests build synthetic books in temporary folders and use a stub embedder, so they need no GGUF model, no converter and no chat server. The two OCR tests in tests/test_convert.py need docling importable; install the ocr group to run them.

Run a single file while working:

uv run pytest tests/test_align.py

docs.title: Comparison scripts
docs.text:
scripts/ holds the scripts used for the measurements in Embedding models:

uv run scripts/compare_lakoff.py BOOK 0 1.05 jina,gemma,granite   # per-language yield, agreement, multi-way units
uv run scripts/compare_models.py BOOK 2000                        # jina vs gemma on a slice, with sample disagreements

scripts/bake_pdf.py timed the PDF converters for the bake-off that chose markit.

docs.title: Code layout
docs.text: module role cli.py The Cli class that Fire turns into commands. config.py Dataclasses for paraltext.toml and the config file search. pipeline.py Book, the four stages and run_all. convert.py PDF, EPUB and DjVu to markdown. ocr.py docling OCR, run as a child process. normalize.py Chunking and the chat-completion client. segment.py Markdown clean-up and sentence splitting. embed.py Adapter to the uubed embedding engine. cache.py diskcache stores for normalized chunks and vectors. align.py Centring, margin mining, overlap resolution, order filter, gap filling. tmx.py TMX writer.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text: The version comes from Git tags through hatch-vcs. A build writes src/vexy_paraltext/_version.py, which is ignored by Git. Without it, vexy_paraltext.__version__ is 0.0.0.dev0.

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
./build.sh            # documentation and package
./build.sh docs       # documentation only: src_docs/md -> docs/
./build.sh package    # package only: dist/*.whl and dist/*.tar.gz, checked with twine

The package build uses uv build --no-sources, so local editable source paths never leak into release metadata.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
The documentation sources are Markdown files in src_docs/md/. ProperDocs with the MaterialX theme builds them into docs/, which GitHub Pages serves at https://vexy.dev/vexy-paraltext/.

src_docs/build.sh         # strict build into docs/
src_docs/build.sh serve   # live preview on http://127.0.0.1:8000

Do not edit docs/ by hand; the next build replaces it. The Docs workflow rebuilds docs/ and commits it on every push to main that changes src_docs/.

docs.title: Release
docs.text:
Prerequisites: review git status and git diff, because the release commits every pending change; push access to origin, and a PyPI credential for uv publish, such as UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN in the environment.

  1. Run the tests:

    ./test.sh

  2. Publish:

    ./publish.sh

    gitnextver commits all pending changes, tags the next vX.Y.Z and pushes. The script then builds the package from that tag with ./build.sh package and uploads dist/* with uv publish.

publish.sh stops if HEAD carries no vX.Y.Z tag afterwards; gitnextver only tags when there is something to commit.

The older gated release helper, scripts/release.py, is still in the repository. It runs the tests, builds in a disposable copy, verifies archive contents and supports --dry-run, --resume vX.Y.Z and --bump. Run it with uv run --no-project --script scripts/release.py --dry-run. See RELEASING.md.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text: This page follows one book through the four stages. The code lives in src/vexy_paraltext/: convert.py, normalize.py, segment.py, embed.py, align.py, tmx.py, with pipeline.py tying them together.

docs.title: Finding the editions
docs.text:
The tool lists the subfolders of the book folder in alphabetical order and keeps each one that:

  • does not start with a dot, and
  • contains at least one .pdf, .epub or .djvu file.

The folder name is the language code. A name made of two or more two-letter codes joined by hyphens, such as de-en, marks a single volume in several languages; such folders are skipped with a warning. zh-hant is one language and is kept.

A book needs at least two editions; otherwise the stage fails with need at least two language editions.

docs.title: Stage 1: convert
docs.text:
Each edition becomes one markdown file next to its source: en/Book.pdf becomes en/Book.md. An existing .md is reused unless --force is given. Editions with a text layer convert in parallel ([convert] workers); editions that need OCR convert one at a time afterwards, because several OCR pipelines side by side ran out of memory.

PDF. The tool first checks for a text layer with PyMuPDF. A PDF counts as text when at least 30% of its pages carry 200 or more characters and the mean is at least 400 characters per page.

  • With a text layer, markit -q --no-images converts it. If markit fails, or its output is less than half the length of PyMuPDF's plain text, the tool uses PyMuPDF's text instead, one paragraph per text block.
  • Without a text layer, docling OCRs it.

For Cyrillic editions (ru, uk, bg, sr, mk, be), text that looks like cp1251 bytes read as Latin-1 is recoded.

EPUB. The external epub2md.py script merges the book into one markdown file in the scratch folder paraltext-cache/epub-<lang>/. If the largest markdown file it writes is smaller than 2000 bytes, the EPUB is treated as image-only: its page images are stacked into a PDF, one image per page, and OCRed. Fewer than eight usable images is an error.

DjVu. djvutxt extracts the text layer; form feeds separate pages. If the text is shorter than 2000 characters, ddjvu -format=pdf -quality=85 renders the file to PDF in paraltext-cache/djvu-<lang>/ and docling OCRs it.

OCR. docling runs in a child process (python -m vexy_paraltext.ocr <pdf> <out.md>). If it crashes, that edition fails with a ConvertError and the rest of the book continues.

docs.title: Stage 2: normalize
docs.text:
When [normalize] enabled = true, the markdown is split on blank lines into chunks of at most chunk_chars characters. A paragraph longer than that is cut at a space. Chunks go to the chat server in parallel with a fixed system prompt that asks the model to:

  • join broken words and stray spaces ("sa me" becomes "same"),
  • turn ALL CAPS and letter-spaced headings into sentence case,
  • drop page numbers, running heads, tables of contents, figure numbers, footnote markers and markdown syntax,
  • keep every sentence, without summarizing or translating.

A failed request is retried three times with 1, 2 and 4 seconds of back-off. An answer cut off by the token limit splits its chunk in two and retries each half, up to three levels deep. Every answer is cached, so an interrupted run resumes where it stopped. The result is <stem>.norm.md.

docs.title: Stage 3: segment and embed
docs.text:
Segmentation (segment.py) turns the markdown into sentences:

  1. Unescape HTML entities, drop soft hyphens, images, link targets and HTML tags.
  2. Rejoin words hyphenated across a line break.
  3. Reflow each paragraph onto one line and strip markdown marks (*, _, `, #, >).
  4. Split with pysbd for languages it supports; other languages, such as pt, tr, ro, cs, lt, hu and sv, use a regex splitter.
  5. Keep sentences of 15 to 600 characters where at least half the characters are letters and at most 20% are digits.
  6. Drop sentences that occur more than twice in the edition: running heads and table-of-contents entries repeat, body sentences do not.

Embedding encodes every sentence and every pair of adjacent sentences. The pairs let one sentence in one edition match two in another. For a 3-sentence edition [s0, s1, s2] the tool embeds s0, s1, s2, s0 s1 and s1 s2.

Vectors are looked up in the cache first; only missing texts go to the model. New vectors are stored at the configured precision.

docs.title: Stage 4: align
docs.text:
Each non-pivot edition is aligned against the pivot, in parallel threads. For one pair of editions:

  1. Centre. With center = true, subtract the mean of all vectors of both editions and renormalize. Without this, a model with a compressed vector space, such as Granite, never clears the margin threshold.
  2. Mine. For every candidate, find its four nearest neighbours on the other side by cosine similarity. A pair is kept when each side is the other's nearest neighbour and its ratio margin reaches threshold. The margin is the pair's cosine divided by the average of both sides' mean similarity to their four neighbours.
  3. Resolve overlaps. Candidates are taken in descending score order; one that reuses a sentence already taken on either side is dropped.
  4. Keep the book order. A longest-increasing-subsequence pass keeps the largest set of links that increase on both sides. A translation keeps the source order, so links that jump backwards are dropped.
  5. Fill gaps. Where exactly one sentence on each side sits unaligned between two links, the two are paired if their cosine is at least gap_min_cos.

A link whose target text equals its source text, ignoring spaces, case and punctuation, is dropped. Bilingual editions often quote the original, and those quotes are not translations.

docs.title: Building the units
docs.text: For each pivot span linked in at least min_langs - 1 other editions, the tool writes one unit containing the pivot text and every linked target text. Spans of two sentences are written as one segment, joined by a space. See TMX output for the file format.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: vexy-paraltext is a Python package with a command-line tool. Text extraction depends on a few external programs that you install separately.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.12 or newer.
  • uv (recommended) or pip.
  • For PDFs with a text layer: markit, an npm package. Requires Node.js.
  • For EPUBs: the epub2md.py script (see EPUB converter).
  • For DjVu: djvulibre (djvutxt and ddjvu).
  • For scanned PDFs and image-only EPUBs: docling (optional, slow).
  • For embedding: at least one GGUF embedding model on disk (see Embedding models).

docs.title: Install the package
docs.text:
From PyPI, as a standalone tool:

uv tool install vexy-paraltext
vexy-paraltext run --help

Or with pip into an existing environment:

pip install vexy-paraltext

From a source checkout, for development:

git clone https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-paraltext.git
cd vexy-paraltext
uv sync
uv run vexy-paraltext run --help

The package depends on uubed[inference], which runs the embedding models, and on llama-cpp-python. On Apple Silicon, llama.cpp uses Metal.

docs.title: Optional MLX runtime
docs.text:
The mlx extra installs uubed's MLX runtime, used by profiles with backend = "mlx":

uv sync --extra mlx                   # source checkout
uv tool install "vexy-paraltext[mlx]" # standalone tool

docs.title: Install the converters
docs.text:
1. Install markit for PDFs with a text layer:

    npm install -g @shiftlabs/markit

  2. Install djvulibre if you have DjVu editions:

    brew install djvulibre

  3. Install docling if you have scanned PDFs, scanned DjVu files or image-only EPUBs. In a source checkout, use the ocr dependency group:

    uv sync --group ocr

    For a standalone tool install, add it to the tool environment:

    uv tool install vexy-paraltext --with docling

    vexy-paraltext runs docling in a child process with the same Python interpreter, so docling must be importable from the environment that runs the tool.

When a converter is missing, the conversion of that edition fails with a message that names the install command. Other editions still convert.

docs.title: EPUB converter
docs.text:
EPUBs are converted by an external script, epub2md.py. The tool looks for it in this order:

  1. The VEXY_EPUB2MD environment variable.
  2. The [convert] epub2md key in paraltext.toml.
  3. The default path ~/bin/epub2md.py.

The script is run as uv run -s <script> <epub> --output_dir <dir> --merge --force, so uv must be on PATH.

docs.title: Check the installation
docs.text:
vexy-paraltext run --help
which markit djvutxt

vexy-paraltext run --help prints the arguments and flags of the run command. which prints the path of each converter that is on PATH.

docs.title: Embedding models
docs.text:
The aligner compares sentences by their embedding vectors, so the embedding model decides how many translations are found. Three local GGUF models are configured out of the box. All three run through llama.cpp, with Metal on Apple Silicon.

profile model prompt prefix weights licence jina (default) jina-embeddings-v5-text-nano, text-matching, Q8_0 Query: CC BY-NC gemma EmbeddingGemma 300M, Q8_0 task: sentence similarity \| query: see the model card granite granite-embedding-311m-multilingual-r2, Q8_0 none Apache 2.0

Select a model per call with --model, or set [embed] model in paraltext.toml. Point each profile at the file on your disk with [embed.models.<name>] path (see Configuration).

docs.title: Which one to use
docs.text:
The models were compared on whole books from a private collection of translated books: Stephen King's On Writing (15 editions), Marshall McLuhan's Understanding Media (13), Alberto Manguel's A History of Reading (10) and Lakoff and Johnson's Metaphors We Live By (6). All runs used English as pivot, threshold 1.05 and centred vectors.

jina gemma granite Strengths Most units that span all editions; never collapses on a language; fastest. 2-8% more pairs on major Western languages and Chinese. Most even across languages; best on Czech, Hungarian and Lithuanian; permissive licence. Weaknesses Non-commercial licence on the weights. Lithuanian yield of 32-42%; weak on Hungarian. About 7% fewer pairs overall; slowest.

Where two models link the same pivot sentence, they pick the same translation 93-100% of the time. The choice of model mostly changes how many sentences are found, not which translation is picked.

Rules of thumb:

  • Use jina when you want units across many editions, or when the set includes smaller languages.
  • Use gemma when all editions are in major Western languages or Chinese and recall matters.
  • Use granite when the weights must carry a permissive licence, or for Baltic and Finno-Ugric languages.

docs.title: King, 15 editions
docs.text: jina gemma granite links over 14 target languages 41,625 41,274 38,901 best on da, ro, sv de, es, it, pl, pt, ru, tr, zh cs, hu, lt units in all 15 editions 176 98 127 units in 10 or more editions 2,362 2,348 2,064 embedding 127k texts 559 s 608 s 701 s

docs.title: McLuhan, 13 editions
docs.text:
jina gemma granite links over 12 target languages 54,349 55,128 51,994 Lithuanian yield 53% 42% 56% units in all 13 editions 422 325 346 units in 10 or more editions 2,971 3,120 2,652

The pattern repeats: gemma edges the totals through the large languages, jina holds every language and wins the all-edition units by 20-30%.

docs.title: Why vectors are centred
docs.text:
Granite's vector space is compressed: random sentence pairs across languages score a cosine of about 0.80 and true translations about 0.97. The best neighbour is then never 5% better than the average neighbour, so the ratio margin never reaches 1.05. On the Lakoff book, Granite found 145 English-Spanish links without centring.

Subtracting the joint mean vector of both editions removes the shared offset. With [embed] center = true, the default, Granite found 2,578 English-Spanish links on the same book, and jina and gemma gained 4-12% as well.

docs.title: Other backends
docs.text: The uubed engine also runs profiles with other backends. The example configuration declares local SentenceTransformers and MLX profiles (nomic, minilm, voyage-nano) and API profiles (jina-api, gemma-api, granite-api, voyage-lite). The API backends read credentials from environment variables. The comparisons above cover only the three GGUF models.

docs.title: Precision and cache size
docs.text: Vectors are stored in the cache at [embed] precision. int8 is the default. In a test run on one EPUB book, float32 and int8 vectors produced 63 units each; 62 were identical and one alignment changed.

docs.title: TMX output
docs.text: The align stage writes a TMX 1.4 file. By default it is <book_dir>/<book_dir name>.tmx; --out sets another path. An existing file is overwritten.

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
The file uses UTF-8, one translation unit per line, and no indentation, so it stays small and diffs line by line:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<tmx version="1.4">
<header creationtool="vexy-paraltext" creationtoolversion="0.1" segtype="sentence" o-tmf="md" adminlang="en" srclang="en" datatype="plaintext"/>
<body>
<tu><tuv xml:lang="en"><seg>He works very hard every day.</seg></tuv><tuv xml:lang="de"><seg>Er arbeitet jeden Tag sehr hart.</seg></tuv><tuv xml:lang="fr"><seg>Il travaille très dur chaque jour.</seg></tuv></tu>
</body>
</tmx>
element content header/@srclang The pivot language. header/@segtype Always sentence. tu One aligned pivot span and its counterparts. tuv/@xml:lang The edition's folder name, for example en, de or zh-hant. seg Plain text.

The pivot tuv comes first in each unit. The others follow in the order of the edition folders.

docs.title: What a unit contains
docs.text:
• A unit has at least min_langs variants (default 2). It never contains empty segments for editions where no translation was found.
  • A segment holds one sentence or two adjacent sentences joined by a space. Two-sentence segments appear when one edition splits a sentence that another keeps whole.
  • Pairs where the "translation" equals the source text, ignoring case, spaces and punctuation, are left out.

docs.title: Text cleaning
docs.text:
Segment text comes from the normalized (or raw) markdown after segmentation, so markdown syntax and HTML tags are already removed. When the file is written:

  • &, < and > in text are escaped.
  • Attribute values are quoted and escaped.
  • Characters that XML 1.0 forbids, such as the control characters U+0000-U+0008, are removed from text and attributes. Tab, line feed, carriage return and all legal Unicode characters, including supplementary-plane ones, are kept.

docs.title: Using the file
docs.text:
TMX 1.4 is read by most CAT tools and translation-memory libraries. Because each unit sits on one line, ordinary text tools work too:

# Count translation units
grep -c '<tu>' book/book.tmx

# Units that include Lithuanian
grep 'xml:lang="lt"' book/book.tmx | wc -l

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: This walk-through builds a TMX from three editions of one book. It skips the LLM clean-up stage, which is the fast path: a heavily illustrated 470-page book takes about five minutes end to end.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• vexy-paraltext and markit installed (see Installation).
  • The default embedding model, jina, downloaded as a GGUF file. The default path is ~/.lmstudio/models/jinaai/jina-embeddings-v5-text-nano-text-matching/v5-nano-text-matching-Q8_0.gguf. If yours is elsewhere, set the path in paraltext.toml (see Configuration).
  • Two or more editions of the same book as PDF, EPUB or DjVu.

docs.title: Build the TMX
docs.text:
1. Create a book folder with one subfolder per language. Use language codes as folder names:

    frutiger/
  en/Typefaces.pdf
  de/Schriften.pdf
  fr/Caracteres.pdf

    Put exactly one edition in each language folder. If a folder holds several, the tool uses the first in alphabetical order and logs a warning.

  2. Create frutiger/paraltext.toml that switches off the LLM stage:

    [normalize]
enabled = false

  3. Run all stages:

    vexy-paraltext run frutiger

    The tool converts the three PDFs to en/Typefaces.md, de/Schriften.md and fr/Caracteres.md, splits them into sentences, embeds them, aligns German and French against English and writes the TMX. The last line of output names the result:

    <number of units> units -> frutiger/frutiger.tmx

  4. Open frutiger/frutiger.tmx in a CAT tool or a text editor. Each line between <body> and </body> is one translation unit.

docs.title: Try settings on a slice
docs.text:
Alignment settings are easier to tune on the first part of a book. The vectors stay in the cache, so a second call only redoes the alignment.

  1. Align the first 2000 sentences of each edition with a stricter threshold, into a separate file:

    vexy-paraltext align frutiger --limit 2000 --threshold 1.1 --out /tmp/slice.tmx

  2. Compare it with the default threshold:

    vexy-paraltext align frutiger --limit 2000 --out /tmp/slice-default.tmx

    A higher threshold gives fewer, cleaner pairs. On the Frutiger book, raising it from 1.05 to 1.1 roughly halved the number of units.

docs.title: Process a whole collection
docs.text:
batch runs run on every book folder under a root folder:

vexy-paraltext batch ~/books

A book that fails is logged and skipped; the batch continues with the next one.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Turn on the LLM clean-up stage for noisier sources: see Configuration.
  • Compare embedding models: see Embedding models.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Messages below are quoted from the code. Add --verbose to any command to see debug logging, including every converter command line.

docs.title: Book-level errors
docs.text:
need at least two language editions in <dir> The book folder has fewer than two subfolders with a .pdf, .epub or .djvu file. Check that each language has its own subfolder. Folders named like de-en are skipped as multilingual volumes and do not count.

fewer than two converted editions in <dir>: run convert first The embed or align stage found markdown for fewer than two editions. Run convert (and normalize if enabled) and check the log for editions that failed.

<path> missing: run convert/normalize first An edition's .md or .norm.md file is missing. With normalize enabled, the stages read <stem>.norm.md; run normalize, or set [normalize] enabled = false.

docs.title: Conversion errors
docs.text:
A failed edition is logged as <book>/<lang>: <message> and skipped; the other editions continue.

message cause fix markit not found; install with: npm install -g @shiftlabs/markit markit is not on PATH. Install it. djvutxt not found; install with: brew install djvulibre djvulibre is missing. Install it. scanned PDF needs docling: uv sync --group ocr A scan needs OCR and docling is not importable. Install docling into the tool's environment. epub2md.py not found at <path>; set VEXY_EPUB2MD The EPUB converter script is missing. Set VEXY_EPUB2MD or [convert] epub2md. <file>: EPUB has no usable text and only <n> page images The EPUB has neither text nor at least eight page images. Use another edition. OCR of <file> failed (exit <code>): ... docling crashed in its child process. Retry; if it repeats, use another edition or convert it by hand (see below).

docs.title: Converting an edition by hand
docs.text: The convert stage skips any edition whose markdown already exists. To work around a converter, write <stem>.md next to the source yourself, for example from another tool's output, and run the remaining stages. Do not pass --force, which would overwrite your file.

docs.title: Few or poor alignments
docs.text:
• Low yield for one language. Check <stem>.md for that edition. Scrambled line order, as in vertically typeset text after OCR, cannot be fixed by the aligner. In the tests, a vertically typeset Traditional Chinese edition aligned at 12% while the Simplified Chinese edition of the same translation aligned at about 50%.
  • Mojibake in a Cyrillic PDF. The tool recodes cp1251 text that was read as Latin-1, but only for folders named ru, uk, bg, sr, mk or be. Name the folder with the right language code.
  • Too many wrong pairs. Raise --threshold, for example to 1.1. Lowering it to 1.0 admits more caption and footnote mismatches.
  • Too few pairs with Granite. Make sure [embed] center is true.
  • English sentences in a non-English edition. Pairs whose target equals the source text are dropped automatically. Other quoted passages can still align.

docs.title: Embedding errors
docs.text:
model file missing: <path> The GGUF file of the selected llama.cpp profile is not at its configured path. Set [embed.models.<name>] path.

unknown model alias or missing GGUF: <name> --model names neither a profile nor an existing file.

GGUF requires a model profile: ... --model points at a GGUF file that no profile declares. Add an [embed.models.<name>] table with path and model, then select it by name.

docs.title: Normalize errors
docs.text: normalize failed after 3 attempts: ... The chat server did not answer. Check that LM Studio (or another OpenAI-compatible server) is running at [normalize] base_url and serves [normalize] model. Answers received before the failure are cached; the next run continues from there.

docs.title: Starting over
docs.text: Delete <book>/paraltext-cache/ to drop cached LLM chunks and vectors. Run convert --force and normalize --force to rebuild the markdown.
